name: Massaman Curry
intro: This curry is famous for a reason. Beef short ribs are simmered until tender, then finished in a rich coconut milk massaman sauce with sweet potato, onion, tamarind, palm sugar, fish sauce, and roasted peanuts.
method: Cut the beef from the bone and, if necessary, cut it into large cubes.
In a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat, add enough oil to cover the bottom, then fry the beef until fully browned on both sides. Do this in batches as needed and avoid overcrowding the pan.
Once all the beef is seared, return it to the pan, together with the bones removed.
Add 1/2 cup coconut milk and enough water to submerge everything.
Add 1 tablespoon curry paste and 1 tablespoon fish sauce, then simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is tender.
In a second heavy-bottomed pot, add about 3/4 cup of the remaining coconut milk and bring to a boil. Let it boil until reduced by half and thickened.
Add the remaining curry paste to the reduced coconut milk over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the coconut oil separates from the curry paste.
Add the remaining coconut milk and stir until the paste dissolves. Add the remaining tamarind juice, palm sugar, and fish sauce.
Use tongs to transfer the beef from the first pot to the curry pot. Leave the bones behind and reserve the cooking liquid.
Add the onion, sweet potato, and roasted peanuts to the curry.
Skim fat and scum from the reserved beef cooking liquid, then add enough liquid to the curry to submerge everything.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender.
Taste and adjust with more fish sauce, sugar, or tamarind as needed.
